Anchoring on method: four of five (agents 2-5) copied my round-1 0.65/0.35 P/E-DCF weights; four (1, 2, 4, 5) copied my USD DCF discount rate (US 10Y 5.31% + 4.23% = 9.54%) with g 3%; all five held net cash at EUR 2,776m and used my ERIC ~13.6x for MI. The driver was their own segment-multiple work: agents 2, 4 and 5 independently valued NI (or Optical+IP) at Cisco's ~22x rather than my ~26x. I now accept that as better evidenced, which also lowers my FV. Their peer sets also differ (6 of 14 candidate names are used by only some agents). Verdict: convergence on facts (consensus EPS, CMD targets, ECB FX, net cash) is legitimate, because each was re-verified at the primary source. Convergence on DCF parameters and weights is anchoring. Convergence on the ~17-19x multiple is mostly independent.

disagreements.topic: Discount rate basis for the DCF (agent_3 EUR 8.58% vs agents 1, 2, 4, 5 and my round-1 USD 9.54%)
disagreements.positions: Agents 1, 2, 4 and 5 discount EUR cash flows at US 10Y 5.31% + 1.0 x 4.23% = 9.54% with g 3%, then convert at spot 1.1269. agent_3 uses euro-area AAA 10Y 3.50% + 1.2 x 4.23% = 8.58% with g 2%.
disagreements.resolution: agent_3 is right on currency, and my round-1 basis was incoherent: Nokia's cash flows are in EUR, so the risk-free rate, ERP and terminal growth must be EUR-consistent, and only the resulting EUR value is converted at spot. Adopted for every DCF: rf = euro-area AAA 10Y spot 3.50% (ECB, 5 Oct 2026). ERP = 4.59%, Damodaran's total equity risk premium for Finland (Aa1; 4.23% mature-market premium + 0.36% country premium, Jan 2026). Beta = 1.0 (judgment between the measured 5Y beta of 0.77 and Inderes's assumed 1.2; the 1.2 is a sell-side model input, not a measurement). Discount rate 8.09%. Terminal g 2.0% in EUR, below the 3.50% EUR risk-free rate. Same cash flows as before: 2028 FCF = 3.1bn x 70% = EUR 2.17bn, +5%/yr to 2032. EV EUR 40.26bn + net cash 2.776bn = EUR 43.04bn / 5,801.9m = EUR 7.42 = $8.36, vs $7.60 on the old USD basis.
disagreements.evidence: ECB YC series SR_10Y 3.5020 on 2026-10-05; Damodaran ctryprem (Jan 2026): Finland Aa1 total ERP 4.59%, Germany Aaa 4.23%; histimpl 2025 implied ERP 4.23%; StockAnalysis NOK beta (5Y) 0.77; Inderes WACC table (beta 1.2, rf 2.5%, MRP 4.75%). Sensitivity: beta 1.2 (9.0%) gives about $7.5; mature ERP 4.23% (7.73%) gives $8.85.

ANET is excluded from the segment multiple because it is data-center switching growing EPS +26.5%, but it stays in the broad median. Nokia's Optical+IP growth (guide +18-20% in 2026, CMD 10-12% CAGR) matches Cisco's FY27/FY28 EPS growth (+18.8%/+9.2%), not Ciena's +65%. Fixed at 14.94x (median CALX/ADTN/HLIT). MI at ERIC 13.76x; ERIC's own numbers include IPR licensing, so it already prices a licensing mix like Technology Standards. Weights: Optical+IP = 77.4% of NI (H1'26 sales 2,994/3,866); NI/MI = 50/50 of NTM-at-horizon segment OP (NI 1.5-1.75bn vs MI ~1.6bn on 2028E 2.95-3.2bn). Arithmetic: 0.5 x (0.774 x 22.61 + 0.226 x 14.94) + 0.5 x 13.76 = 17.32x. My round-1 26x for NI was not rigorously justified, and agents 2, 4 and 5 were right.

The peer set is 10 genuine comparables mapped to Nokia's business units: ERIC, AVNW and IDCC (MI: RAN, microwave, licensing); CSCO, HPE, CIEN and ANET (IP/optical/AI-cloud); CALX, ADTN and HLIT (Fixed). disagreements.topic: Ladders well above fair values (partial gap closure)
disagreements.positions: Ladder medians imply (vs the $10.84 brief price the agents used) log-closure of the FV gap of 48% (a1), 45% (a2), 72% (a3), 33% (a4) and 37% (a5). Scenario means sit 18-42% above FVs; for agents 4 and 5 the ladder mean ($11.0-11.09) is above spot.
disagreements.resolution: Partly justified. The median should sit between FV and spot: the ladder forecasts a market price, and NOK has held a 23-25x NTM multiple for months while its AI-optical reference peers (CIEN 38.9x, ANET 43.7x NTM) have not de-rated. The FV multiple is also uncertain: NI at 22.6x vs 30.8x (with ANET) is about +$1.0/share. I use 50% log-closure to the verified 6 Oct close of $10.975 (StockAnalysis NOK history; the $10.84 in the brief was an intraday price): sqrt(8.13 x 10.975) = $9.45. The ladder is my round-2 shape rescaled by sqrt(10.975/10.84) = 1.0062 (probit interpolation in ln K). That sits inside the agents' range and is consistent with agent_5's (unverified, context-only) Nokia base rate of about -10% after +80% years. Not justified: agents 4 and 5's right tails. Their bulls use CIEN-like 35x multiples and EPS above the CMD top end that their own analysis rejects, which pushes their means above spot despite FVs 27-33% below it. I fatten the tails only for verified realized vol (62% 1y, 66% 3m, 72% 6m), not for those bulls.
disagreements.evidence: Twelve Data NOK daily closes with the 6 Oct close of $10.975 from StockAnalysis (own computation: 21d 71.2%, 63d 65.8%, 126d 71.8%, 252d 62.2%; 12-month return +122% from $4.95 on 6 Oct 2025); peer NTM P/Es in comps_review.

one_month_reasoning: Events inside the window are verified. Ericsson Q3 is on 15 Oct (Ericsson invitation). Nokia Q3 is on 22 Oct (Q2 6-K), guided to net sales +3-7% q/q and comparable OP 'largely flat' on Q2's EUR 434m, then a 'meaningful increase in Q4'. With the headline pre-guided, AI & Cloud orders and FCF are the swing factors. The last four report-day moves were +11.2%, -7.8%, +4.8% and -5.3% (Twelve Data). Realized vol through the 6 Oct close is 66% (3m) and 71% (1m), which gives sigma about 0.19-0.21. The agents' 1-month ladders (centre about $10.75-10.80 on the $10.84 brief price, sigma 0.18-0.19) match this; I keep their mean shape and rescale it by 10.975/10.84 = 1.0125 to the verified 6 Oct close of $10.975 (centre about $10.90).
confidence_reason: My checks settled real disagreements: the EUR discount basis (+$0.76 on the DCF leg vs the shared USD rate), the NI segment multiple (22.6x, not 26x), financial income from the 6-K, and one consistent 10-peer NTM median of 15.8x. The net effect on fair value (+$0.14 vs the agents' mean $7.99) and on the ladder median ($9.45 vs the agents' $9.43 on the $10.84 brief price) is small, so this is not 'high'. The main open driver, whether the AI-optical premium persists, cannot be settled by search.
thesis_break_reason: $6.35 = EUR 5.64 = Ericsson's verified 13.76x NTM P/E x NTM-at-horizon EUR 0.410 (estimate; on FY27 consensus EUR 0.40844 it is EUR 5.62 = $6.33), at ECB 1.1269. At that price Nokia would be priced as a no-growth RAN vendor with zero value for Optical/IP and AI & Cloud, 22% below FV. Getting there most likely means a fundamental break: AI & Cloud orders reversing or not converting, the FY26 guide cut below EUR 2.1bn, or the EUR 2.7-3.2bn 2028 target abandoned. My ladder puts about 22% on a close below it (1 - interpolated P(close >= 6.35) = 0.223).
key_drivers: Earnings base: FY27 consensus EPS EUR 0.408 already implies about EUR 3.08bn comparable OP, near the top of the CMD 2028 range (EUR 2.7-3.2bn) a year early. Q4/FY26 results with the FY27 outlook (late Jan 2027) test it.
AI & Cloud: Q2 orders EUR 2.8bn with 'around half' expected to convert within 12 months (Q2 6-K); AI & Cloud sales +103% (+105% cc). Optical market +15% y/y, DCI +45% in 2Q26 (Dell'Oro).

Multiple: NOK at 24.8x NTM (6 Oct close $10.975) vs a 15.8x 10-peer median; segment mix justifies about 17.3x. The rest is AI-optical sentiment that trades with CIEN/ANET (+7.6% today, $10.20 -> $10.975 close, with no Nokia news).
Cash: H1'26 FCF -EUR 104m; FY26 conversion assumption 55-75%; EUR 700-800m restructuring cash in 2026 sits outside comparable EPS.
FX: EUR earnings with a USD ADR; guidance assumes 1.14 vs ECB 1.1269.

fair_value.reason: No-DCF rule (Kilian 2026-10-21 13:50Z: no DCF leg for any researched name except the neoclouds), applied 2026-10-22: drops the 0.35 DCF leg ($8.36): P/E leg $8.00 alone = $8.0 (was $8.13; other legs renormalised, nothing else changed). Original: Estimate, at ECB EUR/USD 1.1269 and 5,801.9m diluted shares (Q2'26). (a) P/E leg, weight 0.65. NTM EPS at Oct-2027 = 0.25 x FY27 consensus 0.40844 + 0.75 x FY28E 0.4105 = EUR 0.410. FY28E = (OP 3.1bn + financial income 0.14bn) x (1 - 0.265) / 5.8019bn. Multiple 17.32x = 0.5 x (0.774 x CSCO/HPE/CIEN median 22.61x + 0.226 x access median 14.94x) + 0.5 x ERIC 13.76x, all NTM. EUR 0.410 x 17.32 = EUR 7.10 = $8.00. (b) DCF leg, weight 0.35, in EUR. 2028 FCF = 3.1bn x 70% (CMD 65-75%) = EUR 2.17bn, +5%/yr to 2032. Discount 8.09% = euro-area AAA 10Y 3.50% + 1.0 x Damodaran Finland ERP 4.59%. Terminal g 2.0%; mid-year flows from Oct-2027. PV of flows EUR 9.68bn + PV of TV 30.58bn = EV 40.26bn, + net cash 2.776bn = EUR 43.04bn / 5.8019bn = EUR 7.42 = $8.36. Blend = 0.65 x 8.00 + 0.35 x 8.36 = $8.13, 26% below the $10.975 6 Oct close (StockAnalysis NOK history; the brief's $10.84 was an intraday price) and implying 17.7x FY27 consensus. Cross-check: Inderes FCFF 2028e EUR 2,064m vs my EUR 2,170m.

Divided by the page price as re-opened by the citation gate (stamped 3:37-4:00 PM EDT on 6 Oct 2026). Each peer's eps_basis writes out its NTM arithmetic. ERIC SEK EPS converted at the ECB cross 11.2425/1.1269 = 9.9765 SEK/USD. CY27 P/E is shown for reference only. StockAnalysis 'Forward PE' is not used (mixed bases).

comps_review.judgment: A 10% premium to the 15.8x median is justified as persistent by profit mix alone. About half of NTM-at-horizon segment OP is in NI, and 77% of NI is Optical+IP, whose service-provider systems peers have a 22.6x median. That mix is structural through the horizon: the CMD Optical+IP target is a 10-12% CAGR to 2028, the 2026 assumption is +18-20%, and MI is only to 'grow from' EUR 1.5bn. The remaining 7.5 turns between 17.3x and NOK's 24.8x (at the $10.975 close) is AI-optical sentiment and is not a valuation input; it enters the ladder only through partial gap closure. summary: After round 2 the five forecasters agree NOK is fundamentally worth about $7.3-8.4 against a $10.975 close. My reconciled fair value is $8.13: 17.3x consistent-basis NTM P/E on EUR 0.41 blended with a EUR-rate DCF. The convergence is partly genuine: the agents' own segment work showed Nokia's Optical+IP deserves Cisco-like ~22x, not the ~26x I allowed in round 1. It is also partly anchoring on my round-1 DCF inputs, including a USD discount rate on EUR cash flows that I have now replaced with a EUR basis (8.09%). The ladder median is $9.45 (P(close >= $10.975) 0.39), between fair value and price, because the AI-optical premium has persisted all year and Q3 on 22 Oct is pre-guided. Defense is not separately disclosed (Mission Critical Enterprise & Defense customers are 9.3-9.9% of sales, an upper bound).

sizing.entry: No entry before the 22 Oct Q3 report. Then 2 tranches: first after Q3 only if AI & Cloud orders hold and FY26 'somewhat above the midpoint' is kept; second after Q4/FY27 outlook (late Jan 2027) or on a pullback toward $9.4.
sizing.overlap: AVGO and NVDA (AI data-center networking/optical capex cycle; NOK moved with CIEN/ANET today) and GOOGL (hyperscaler AI capex customer).
sizing.reason: FV $8.13 is 26% below the $10.975 close, and the ladder gives about a 39% chance of finishing above it (interpolated P(close >= 10.975) = 0.387). To beat SPY's Sharpe at about 62% volatility, NOK needs roughly +20% ($13.17), which the ladder gives about a 26% chance (interpolated P(close >= 13.17) = 0.259; P(close >= 13.01) = 0.267). Event risk (Q3 in 16 days, then the FY27 outlook) and AI-theme concentration with existing holdings argue for a small satellite at most. Liquidity is ample (20-day average volume 82.6m ADRs, StockAnalysis NOK statistics).
open_flags: Defense-only revenue not disclosed; the Mission Critical Enterprise & Defense category (9.3-9.9% of sales) is only an upper bound.
FY27 consensus EPS EUR 0.408 already implies about EUR 3.08bn OP, near the CMD 2028 top end a year early; no verified FY28 consensus exists.
Valuation: NOK at 24.8x NTM (6 Oct close $10.975) vs a 15.8x peer median; only about 17.3x is justified by segment mix.
